title: A Group Chat for the Playlist
premise: Lena Vane, a quiet coder who hides behind an anonymous account, discovers her late grandmother's recipe box contains coded instructions for the town's century-old Founders' Playlist—a tradition of songs passed down each spring that is about to be discontinued by a school board eager to modernize. Following the recipes' clues, Lena uncovers that her grandmother secretly curated the playlist for decades and left it to whoever could decode it. With help from Theo, a transfer student who stumbles into her secret, Lena must reconstruct the final playlist and defend it at the last audition before the tradition ends—learning that belonging means carrying memory forward, not keeping it hidden.
about_author: Hazel Ravensworth grew up in a small river town where every summer ended with a community concert on the courthouse steps, an experience that shaped her love of stories about place and inheritance. She writes young adult fiction from a cluttered desk overlooking a train line, where she collects old recipe boxes and the secrets tucked inside them.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. We meet Lena navigating school invisibly: perfect code, closed locker, anonymous online handle 'quietfreq' where she's oddly candid. Establishes her loneliness as a choice. Emotional beat: safety in silence, with a hairline crack of wanting more.

chapters.title: The Box on the Top Shelf
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. After grandma Ruth's funeral, Lena inherits the recipe box. Sorting cards to feel close to her, she finds one labeled 'For the Spring Set' containing musical notation and odd measurements. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into curiosity.

chapters.title: Measurements That Aren't Cups
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She realizes the card's numbers map to song lengths and years, not ingredients. Cross-referencing with the town archive's mention of the Founders' Playlist, her pulse quickens. Emotional beat: the thrill of a puzzle only she can see.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Read Over My Shoulder
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. New student Theo glimpses Lena's notes in study hall and asks the wrong-right question: 'Is that a recipe or a setlist?' Lena shuts down, but he leaves a napkin sketch of a treble clef on her desk. Emotional beat: unwanted attention that feels dangerously like being seen.

chapters.title: Locker Shut, Door Open
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena tests Theo with a fake clue; he solves it without showing off. She admits, in her anonymous forum voice typed aloud, what she found. Emotional beat: cautious alliance formed over shared outsider status.

chapters.title: A Tradition Nobody Under Eighty Remembers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They research the Founders' Playlist: since 1921, graduating seniors performed inherited songs at the spring assembly. This year the board votes to replace it with a 'modern showcase.' Emotional beat: urgency—the clock is real.

chapters.title: Card Number Seven
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Card seven references 'the year the river took the bridge,' leading them to 1948 newspaper microfilm and a photo of young Ruth holding a violin. Emotional beat: grandmother transformed from memory into person.

chapters.title: The Anonymous Account Knows Too Much
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Someone messages 'quietfreq': 'Ask your box about the bridge.' A stranger is watching her decode. Paranoia spikes; Theo suspects a rival decoder. Emotional beat: her sanctuary turned surveillance.

chapters.title: Mrs. Okonkwo's Basement Archive
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The retired music teacher lets them into her basement of program booklets going back decades. She recognizes Ruth's handwriting instantly—and goes pale at card seven. Emotional beat: adults carry their own unfinished griefs.

chapters.title: What Grandma Never Played
chapters.summary: Mrs. Okonkwo reveals Ruth was supposed to inherit curatorship in 1949 but refused after her sister drowned—the bridge year. The playlist skipped her. Emotional beat: the wound beneath the recipe box.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the packed board meeting, the modernization passes 5–2. One dissenter, Mr. Aldous, slips Lena a note: 'Your grandmother would have fought.' Emotional beat: public defeat, private summons.

chapters.title: Decoding the Bridge Year
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Using the drowning date as a cipher key, Lena cracks the cards' sequence: twelve songs, each tied to a town event, ending with an unperformed thirteenth—Ruth's own composition, 'For Marisol.' Emotional beat: awe curdling into responsibility.

chapters.title: Thirteen
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The thirteenth song was never played because Ruth couldn't bear to finish it after Marisol died. Theo argues they should perform it anyway; Lena refuses—it feels like grave-robbing. Emotional beat: first real fight between them.

chapters.title: The Stranger in the Forum
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The anonymous messenger escalates: they claim to be another grandchild of a former curator, competing to restore 'their' version of the playlist. Emotional beat: rivalry reframes the quest—not just saving a tradition, but deciding whose memory counts.

chapters.title: Two Boxes
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The rival, Priya Chandrasekaran, granddaughter of curator Elias Ford, shows up at the library with her own recipe box. Her cards are older, more complete—but missing the thirteenth song. Emotional beat: grudging respect between heirs.

chapters.title: Whose Memory Is It Anyway
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya explains her grandfather spent forty years curating while Ruth stayed silent out of guilt. From Priya's side, Ruth abandoned the tradition. Emotional beat: Lena's hero narrative cracks; inheritance is messier than legacy.

chapters.title: The Audition Clause
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Buried in the board's new policy: if students present a 'historically complete' playlist by the final audition date, the tradition survives one more cycle. A loophole—deliberate? Mr. Aldous won't say. Emotional beat: hope with fine print.

chapters.title: Rehearsal of Strangers
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The three rivals plus Mrs. Okonkwo attempt a joint reconstruction; egos and grief collide over which version of song four is 'true.' Emotional beat: collaboration as friction, not harmony.

chapters.title: Marisol's Violin
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Mrs. Okonkwo produces Marisol's violin, kept in storage since 1948, strings never replaced. Lena holds it and finally understands why Ruth stopped. Emotional beat: grief made physical, almost unbearable.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the rebuilt bridge site, Lena reads Ruth's final card aloud: 'Some songs are apologies.' The group realizes the playlist's true purpose was always repair. Emotional beat: purpose revealed—this is about reconciliation, not nostalgia.

chapters.title: Priya's Missing Verse
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya admits her box is incomplete because Elias deliberately omitted the bridge-year songs—he thought forgetting was mercy. Emotional beat: two curators, two philosophies of memory, both loving and both wrong.

chapters.title: The Compromise Draft
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo drafts a merged playlist honoring both boxes, but Lena catches him quietly cutting the thirteenth song 'to keep the peace.' Betrayal lands hard. Emotional beat: even allies edit history when it's easier.

chapters.title: Silence Is Also a Choice
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena confronts her own hypocrisy: she's hidden behind anonymity her whole life, exactly like Ruth hid behind silence. She posts publicly on 'quietfreq' for the first time, revealing her identity. Emotional beat: terrifying liberation.

chapters.title: The Post That Went Around Town
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Lena's post goes viral locally; dozens of elders come forward with fragments—sheet music in attics, a recording on a wire spool. The playlist grows beyond any single box. Emotional beat: the town remembers itself.

chapters.title: The Wire Recording
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. An elderly donor's spool contains a 1949 rehearsal: young Ruth playing 'For Marisol,' incomplete, stopping mid-phrase with a sob. Lena transcribes what exists. Emotional beat: intimacy across seventy years.

chapters.title: Finishing Ruth's Song
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo composes a completion of the thirteenth song using Ruth's harmonic patterns, presenting it humbly—not as his, but as 'the ending she couldn't write.' Lena listens alone, then says yes. Emotional beat: forgiveness through craft.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Days before the audition, the merged score disappears from the library copier queue and Mrs. Okonkwo's basement floods from a 'burst pipe.' Someone wants the tradition dead quietly. Emotional beat: stakes turn sinister.

chapters.title: Who Benefits
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Suspicion falls on board member Ms. Greer, whose family lost face in a 1960s playlist scandal—or on Priya, whose box would win solo. Trust frays among the three. Emotional beat: paranoia threatens the alliance.

chapters.title: Priya Didn't Do It
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya proves her innocence with timestamps and, more importantly, chooses solidarity: she hands Lena Elias's private letters, including his deathbed regret about omitting the bridge songs. Emotional beat: rivalry dissolved into co-custody.

chapters.title: The Backup in the Cloud
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena's coding saves them: she'd encrypted a backup weeks ago, paranoid habit paying off. But restoring it means revealing her methods to the board—including her anonymous account's full history. Emotional beat: privacy traded for the mission.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At an emergency hearing, Lena testifies, decoding live before the board, explaining the cipher, the boxes, the omissions. Ms. Greer watches too carefully. Emotional beat: the invisible girl becomes undeniable.

chapters.title: Ms. Greer's Confession
chapters.summary: Greer's POV (brief). Confronted privately, Greer admits the sabotage—her father was disgraced when the 1963 playlist excluded his immigrant community's songs. She wanted the whole tradition buried. Emotional beat: villain revealed as another wounded heir.

chapters.title: An Apology Seventy Years Long
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The group revises the final playlist to include the 1963 excluded songs alongside the original twelve and Ruth's finished thirteenth. The tradition's flaw becomes its amendment. Emotional beat: inheritance includes repairing what you receive.

chapters.title: Night Before
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Final preparations; the auditorium fills with borrowed instruments. Lena can't sleep and finds Theo doing the same in the empty hall. Quiet conversation about fear, fathers, futures. Emotional beat: tenderness without declaration.

chapters.title: The Final Audition
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The performance: twelve historical songs, the restored 1963 additions, then 'For Marisol,' completed, played on her violin. The room weeps. The board, bound by the clause and moved past it, reinstates the tradition permanently. Emotional beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: What the Audience Didn't See
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Backstage, Greer approaches Lena—not forgiven, but handing over her father's excluded sheet music for next year's curation. Emotional beat: grace extended cautiously, healing begun not finished.

chapters.title: Passing It On
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The three agree to co-curate: two boxes, one playlist, rotating stewardship. Mrs. Okonkwo formally transfers the archive. Priya asks Lena to teach her the cipher. Emotional beat: succession as friendship.

chapters.title: quietfreq, Signed Off
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena archives her anonymous account with a final post: 'Found what I was looking for. It had a name the whole time.' She keeps the handle but stops hiding behind it. Emotional beat: identity integrated, not discarded.

chapters.title: Recipe Box, Refilled
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena adds new cards to Ruth's box—next year's clues, written in her own hand, for whoever inherits next. She visits the bridge and plays the thirteenth song once, just for the river. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into gift.

chapters.title: Encore
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, epilogue. One year later: the spring assembly, larger than ever, Theo composing, Priya archiving, Lena curating. A nervous freshman asks how the playlist works. Lena smiles and hands her a recipe card. Emotional beat: belonging achieved by making room for the next one.
